newsitem.title: POLAND: Solidarity union blasts Polish energy price rises.
newsitem.headline: Solidarity union blasts Polish energy price rises.

text.p: Poland's Solidarity trade union on Tuesday criticised the government decision to raise utility prices by 10-18 percent on January 1, saying the move would hit many households and upset efforts to limit inflation.

Solidarity chairman Marian Krzaklewski told a news conference the union was critical both of the price rises' scope and their timing, as they would come at a time when many households experience a temporary drop in real incomes.
"Such a high scale of increases will be painful for all households because of a recurring drop in incomes in January," Krzaklewski said.
"Solidarity calls on the government to reconsider the timetable and the scope of 1997 increases," he said.
"Such a scale of increases in the context of the ambitious plan to cut inflation to 13 percent in 1997 is seen as absurd," Krzaklewski added.

Krzaklewski suggested that the government should have spread the increases, ranging from 10 percent for hot water and central heating to 15-17.5 percent for electricity and 18 percent for heating gas, over two stages in 1997.
But he said it was reluctant to do so because a second rise would then come shortly before parliamentary polls scheduled for the fourth quarter of 1997.
Solidarity has formed an alliance with centre-right parties to challenge the ruling ex-communists in the elections.

The government said the increases were necessary because the value added tax on the energy products would grow to 17 percent from the current 12 percent next year and because costs of their import, excavation and delivery were rising.
